description: Official LuciferCore framework: A high-performance, fully asynchronous .NET ecosystem designed for Modulith architectures. Fuses Data-Oriented Design (DOD) with high-speed OOP pooling to achieve zero-allocation pipelines and maximum CPU cache locality. Powered by a lock-free Buffer-Model architecture and a lightweight static DI container designed to fully saturate multi-core hardware. Automating infrastructure so you can focus 100% on core logic.
releaseNotes:
feat(core): auto-scan and auto-register plugins by Order, no manual registration needed

      Previously LuciferPlugin only SCANNED classes tagged with [Plugin] to
      build a Type map (Name -> Type) during its static constructor, while
      actual REGISTRATION (creating the instance in the DI container) had
      to be called explicitly via Lucifer.AddPluginsSingleton(...) /
      AddPlugins(...) somewhere in Program.cs (e.g. DIContainer.Configure()).

      Problem: simply touching the `Lucifer` type for the first time (no
      matter which method is called) forces the CLR to run static Lucifer()
      to completion first - and that cctor itself eagerly forces
      RouteHandler's cctor to run inside it to preload all Handlers.
      => RouteHandler tries to resolve Handler dependencies (Service/Storage)
      before AddPlugins ever gets a chance to register anything, if the
      registration call is missed or ordered incorrectly.
      => Runtime failure: "No instance registered for type X", hard to trace
      since the real exception gets wrapped in several layers of
      TargetInvocationException.

      Changes:
      - Merged SCAN and REGISTER into a single step, running directly inside
      LuciferPlugin's static constructor (no more manual AddPlugins call -
      tagging a class with [Plugin] is now enough to get it registered
      automatically).
      - Added PluginAttribute.Order (int, default 0) to control registration
      order; plugins are sorted by Order before being registered, so a
      dependency (e.g. VaultService) is always constructed before the
      plugin that depends on it (e.g. TransitService), instead of relying
      on the arbitrary Type enumeration order of Utf8Map/reflection.
      - Added PluginAttribute.Lifetime (defaults to Singleton) - each plugin
      now registers under exactly ONE lifetime, avoiding accidental
      double-instantiation from registering both Singleton and Transient
      for the same class.
      - Wrapped each plugin registration in its own try/catch: a single
      plugin failing (e.g. constructor throws) now only logs a warning
      instead of taking down the entire scan/app.

      Breaking change:
      - Removed [ConsoleCommand("/init di")] / DIContainer.Configure() -
      no longer needed; calling it again is now a no-op since plugins are
      already registered at app startup.
      - Plugins with cross-dependencies MUST declare an increasing Order
      matching their dependency chain, otherwise the same register-order
      bug can still occur.
title: LuciferCore by thuangf45: High-Performance Zero-Allocation Framework
